messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: The most important interactions with spironolactone are medicines that also raise potassium.
The combined effect of these medicines can push your potassium level dangerously high.
Tell your doctor about every medicine you take, including anything you start or stop during treatment.
Be especially careful with:
eplerenone, which should not be taken with spironolactone at all;
medicines that raise potassium, including ACE inhibitors such as lisinopril and ramipril, ARBs such as losartan and valsartan, NSAIDs, heparin and low molecular weight heparin, and trimethoprim;
potassium supplements and potassium-containing salt substitutes, which are usually stopped when spironolactone is started for heart failure;
Spironolactone slows how fast your kidneys clear spironolactone.
Spironolactone can cause lithium toxicity.
Lithium levels need monitoring.
Digoxin needs care for two separate reasons.
Spironolactone interferes with one type of blood test used to measure digoxin.
Spironolactone can raise the actual amount of digoxin in your body.
Triples: [["spironolactone", "interacts with", "medicines that raise potassium"], ["spironolactone", "has warning", "combined effect can push potassium level dangerously high"], ["spironolactone", "has administration instruction", "tell your doctor about every medicine you take including anything you start or stop during treatment"], ["spironolactone", "should be avoided with", "eplerenone"], ["spironolactone", "interacts with", "ACE inhibitors"], ["spironolactone", "interacts with", "lisinopril"], ["spironolactone", "interacts with", "ramipril"], ["spironolactone", "interacts with", "ARBs"], ["spironolactone", "interacts with", "losartan"], ["spironolactone", "interacts with", "valsartan"], ["spironolactone", "interacts with", "NSAIDs"], ["spironolactone", "interacts with", "heparin"], ["spironolactone", "interacts with", "low molecular weight heparin"], ["spironolactone", "interacts with", "trimethoprim"], ["spironolactone", "interacts with", "potassium supplements"], ["spironolactone", "interacts with", "potassium-containing salt substitutes"], ["spironolactone", "has administration instruction", "usually stop potassium supplements and potassium-containing salt substitutes when spironolactone is started for heart failure"], ["spironolactone", "has mechanism of action", "slows how fast your kidneys clear spironolactone"], ["spironolactone", "has side effect", "can cause lithium toxicity"], ["spironolactone", "requires monitoring of", "lithium levels"], ["spironolactone", "interferes with", "blood test used to measure digoxin"], ["spironolactone", "interacts with", "digoxin"], ["spironolactone", "has effect on drug level", "can raise actual amount of digoxin in your body"]]
Relations: ["has administration instruction", "has effect on drug level", "has mechanism of action", "has side effect", "has warning", "interacts with", "interferes with", "requires monitoring of", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:

completion:
has administration instruction: The subject drug requires the patient to follow the specific instructions related to medication use specified by the object entity.  
has effect on drug level: The subject drug can alter the concentration or effectiveness of the drug specified by the object entity in the body.  
has mechanism of action: The subject drug functions through the physiological or biochemical process specified by the object entity.  
has side effect: The subject drug may cause the adverse effect specified by the object entity.  
has warning: The subject drug is associated with a specific caution or risk that patients should be aware of, as specified by the object entity.  
interacts with: The subject drug may have a combined effect or interaction with the substance or drug specified by the object entity.  
interferes with: The subject drug may affect or disrupt the accuracy or function of the test or process specified by the object entity.  
requires monitoring of: The subject drug necessitates regular monitoring of the parameter or condition specified by the object entity.  
should be avoided with: The subject drug should not be used in conjunction with the substance or drug specified by the object entity.
